description: A cosy colouring book for adults who love books: forty bookish places to colour, from a bookshop in the storm to a blanket fort, each with its own little story.
h1: For readers who say “just one more chapter”
lead: A cosy colouring book for book lovers, with forty bookish places to colour, each with its own little story.
for: For readers with a to-be-read pile taller than they are
For bookshop wanderers and library lovers
For a gift for the friend who always has a book on the go

problem.h: Some nights your eyes are too tired to read
p: You want the cosy feeling of a good book, but it’s late, the words are swimming, and the phone is right there.
Scrolling never gives you the same calm as turning a page.

approach.h: Colour the places books take you
p: Every page is a bookish little world: a bookshop in a storm, a teetering to-be-read tower, a little free library at the end of a lane, a blanket fort with a sleeping dog.
It’s the same slow, calm feeling as reading, for the nights when you’d rather hold a pencil.

offer.p: Detailed, cosy line art for grown-ups who love books.
features: Bookshops, reading nooks, libraries and blanket forts, each with a name.
Every scene has a title and a small story of its own to find in the detail.
A big 8.5 × 11 in page, so there’s space for fine detail.

gallery: A bookshop in a storm, a secret library, a laundry pile losing to an audiobook
Ten of the forty chapters to colour
A little story on the left, your picture on the right
For the book club and for the 2 a.m. reader

proof.p: These are the actual line drawings, straight from the printed book.
note: I made this one for every reader who has said “just one more chapter” at midnight. The Washing Can Wait is my kind of page.
Every picture is printed on its own page, so you can colour with pens or pencils.

items: A mix of simpler and fuller designs

points: One paperback book, printed and posted by Amazon.
No subscription and nothing to download. Open it and start.
Amazon handles delivery and returns, just like anything else you buy there.

faq: Is it like A Cup of Somewhere Else?
It’s in the same cosy style, but every scene is about books and reading. A Cup of Somewhere Else is about places to escape to.
Yes, it’s designed for adults, with fine detail. Older children who love detailed colouring may enjoy it too.
Colouring pencils give the softest results. Gel pens and fine liners are lovely for small details.
Will it be a good gift?
For a book lover, absolutely. It pairs nicely with a reading light or a book.

close.p: Then just one more chapter. Or one more page.
